transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… lately I feel like I’m always going from one thing to the next. Like I can’t really just sit and idle. With the new setup at work, it’s been harder to sort of keep that under wraps, so… that’s why I came in.
Can you tell me more about what it feels like when you can’t sit still or idle—does it feel uncomfortable, or like you always need to be doing something?

Yeah… it’s more like I always need to be doing something. If I’m just sitting there, I start looking for the next thing to handle or move on to. It’s not dramatic, I guess, but it’s uncomfortable to just… idle. At work now, with the new setup, it’s harder to cover that up.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting, tapping your hands or feet, or moving around even when you’re supposed to stay seated, like in meetings or when you're trying to relax?
Yeah… I do that some. Even when I’m trying to seem calm, my foot’ll be bouncing under the desk, or I’ll be clicking a pen in a meeting and not really notice until someone looks over.
Do you find it hard to stay focused on tasks, or do you often start things but have trouble finishing them?

Yeah, sometimes. Like in longer coaching meetings, or if I’m reading a new procedure… I start off okay, but after a few minutes I’ll realize my eyes were moving over it and I didn’t really take much in.
Looking back, were you someone who had trouble staying focused or felt restless as a child, even before your current work stress?

Yeah… I think it was there before all this. I don’t remember every detail, but in grade school my teachers would write things like I was bright but careless, or that I talked out of turn. And I had to be reminded to stay on my work. So… yeah, it wasn’t just this job change.
Can you think of times outside of work—like at home or with friends—where you’ve noticed the same restlessness or trouble staying focused?

Yeah… at home too, I guess. If I’m trying to read or watch a movie with my wife, I don’t usually sit still through the whole thing. I’ll start shifting around, make comments, or get up for something. Not all the time, but enough that I notice it.
Have you ever felt like you talk excessively, or have trouble waiting your turn in conversations or activities, like you jump in before others are done talking?

Yeah… I guess I do that sometimes. At work, if I hear coworkers trying to figure out a customer issue, I’ll jump in with the answer before they’re really done talking, or before they even asked me. I don’t mean it to come off rude, but… yeah, it happens.
Can you think of other situations—like when you’re at home, running errands, or socializing—where you’ve noticed the same trouble staying focused or feeling restless?

Yeah… I mean, if I’m sitting through something slow, like a training video or waiting at an appointment, I start feeling kind of boxed in. Like I need to stand up, stretch, or at least be doing something with my hands. Not every second, but it’s there.
Can you describe how much these feelings of restlessness and trouble focusing have impacted your work, relationships, or daily life?

Mostly at work, I guess. It’s not like I can’t do the job, but it’s been coming up in my reviews more… unfinished tickets, little mistakes that end up slowing other people down. I do try hard, and I get along with customers okay, but… yeah, it’s starting to show.
